text:
The Portugal Embassy in Seoul introduced Korean classical music lovers to the 2027 Marvão International Music Festival, inviting them to experience unique cultural celebration set in one of Portugal's most picturesque destinations.
Nestled nearly 800 meters above sea level in the Alentejo region, close to the Spanish border, Marvão is a small medieval village surrounded by stone walls and a castle. Overlooking the vast landscape of the Serra de São Mamede Natural Park, the hilltop town is widely regarded as one of the most beautiful places in Portugal.
Once a remote medieval stronghold, Marvão has transformed to an international destination for classical music lovers for summer time since German conductor Christoph Poppen fell in love with the place.
"Marvão has medieval walls and a castle, and for centuries it was a fortress built to keep people out. But then a German conductor fell in love with Marvão and did the opposite. He opened its gates to the world," Portuguese Ambassador to Korea Vanda Sequeira said during the event at the ambassadorial residence of Portugal, Tuesday.
With the idea to add a piece of music to silence, Poppen founded the festival with his wife, soprano Juliane Banse, in 2014. Since its inaugural edition, the festival has grown into one of Portugal's largest classical music festivals, while preserving the intimate atmosphere of its historic setting.
Offering a glimpse of the festival's musical atmosphere, the Novus String Quartet played works by Joseph Haydn and Antonín Dvořák at the ambassador's residence, filling the venue with the rich sounds of classical chamber music.
Poppen highlighted the remarkable transformation the event would again bring to the tiny village with just 97 residents.
"During the 10-day festival in July, we bring between 10,000 and 15,000 people from all over the world. We have 32 concerts in 10 days," he said, highlighting the contrast between the village's quiet life throughout the year and its vibrant cultural scene each summer.
Sequeira highlighted the cultural affinity between Portugal and Korea, despite the geographical distance separating the two countries. Drawing a parallel between Portugal's "saudade" — a distinctive sense of longing and melancholy — and Korea's "han," she said both cultures share a deep appreciation for tradition and music.
"Korean musicians now shine on the great stages of the world. I hope many Korean music lovers will also discover a small stage on top of a mountain in Portugal," the ambassador said.
The 2027 Marvão International Music Festival will take place from July 23 to Aug. 1, 2027.
